extracted.intended_audience: journalists, journalism educators, student newsroom staff, and newsrooms interested in practicing solutions journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting rigorous, evidence-based, and audience-relevant news stories that focus on responses to social problems and what can be learned from their successes and failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions journalism is rigorous and compelling reporting about responses to social problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement frames the practice: reporting should center on responses (not just the problem), be evidence-based (rigorous), and be presented in a way that engages audiences (compelling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Focuses on a response to a social problem — and on how that response has worked, or why it hasn’t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story must center on a specific response (program, policy, practice, innovation, community effort) and evaluate its effectiveness or lack thereof, rather than only describing the underlying problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows what can be learned from a response and why it matters to a newsroom’s audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should extract generalizable lessons or takeaways from the response, explaining relevance and implications for readers or the community; connect the particular example to broader issues of interest to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides data or qualitative results that indicate effectiveness (or a lack thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quantitative measures, rigorous qualitative findings, before/after comparisons, or other indicators that support claims about whether the response worked. Avoid anecdote-only claims; document outcomes and be transparent about methods and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Places responses in context; doesn’t shy away from revealing shortcomings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good solutions story acknowledges constraints, trade-offs, root causes that remain, scalability questions, costs, and any weaknesses or failures of the response—providing a balanced, contextualized picture rather than uncritical promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness of responses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat responses themselves as legitimate subjects for news coverage — not just as PR or success stories — when they illuminate solutions, generate lessons, or have implications for the audience. Decide news value based on relevance, novelty, impact potential, and ability to inform action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and compelling storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting should be both rigorous and compelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine rigorous evidence-gathering and critical evaluation with narrative elements (human stories, clear structure, multimedia) that engage readers. Avoid sacrificing analytic rigor for feel-good storytelling; likewise, avoid dry presentation that loses audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multimedia and distribution to maximize reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Use text, videos, photos, graphics and audio across platforms to attract buy-in from different audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The New Vision example shows publishing across print, website, Facebook, X and YouTube increased reach and engagement. Consider platform-tailored packages, visuals and shareable assets to amplify impact and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show measurable impact and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Document audience and community engagement and measurable outcomes (e.g., impressions, views, shares, changes in policy or practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact metrics—such as unusually high views, social shares, or direct responses from officials—can demonstrate that a story influenced discourse or action. Reporters should collect and report such evidence when available to show the real-world effect of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement & collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage communities and stakeholders; build relationships that enable follow-up, accountability, and action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include working with local agencies (e.g., housing authorities), hosting public events to discuss findings, and collaborating with community organizations to ensure reporting reflects local realities and contributes to civic conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing policy, planning, and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should be capable of informing government action, planning processes, or institutional decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact examples show officials citing solutions journalism in planning and policy discussions; thus, reporting should surface actionable insights and evidence that policymakers and practitioners can use, while remaining independent and evidence-focused.
